tools.name: list_structure
tools.description: Return the novel's binder tree: parts, chapters, and scenes with their ids, titles, status, POV, synopsis, and word counts. Call this first to orient yourself in the project.

tools.name: read_unit
tools.description: Read the full prose of a scene, chapter, or part by its unit id (from list_structure). Reading a container concatenates its scenes in order.

tools.name: get_scene_handoff
tools.description: Tail of the scene that PRECEDES the given unit in narrative order — call before drafting so consecutive scenes join without a seam (voice, time of day, open threads).

unitId.description: Unit id of the scene ABOUT to be drafted (from list_structure).

tools.name: search_manuscript
tools.description: Fast text or regex search across every file in the project (prose, bible, notes). Use this to find where characters, objects, or phrases appear before making claims or edits. For a character or place, pass `entity` instead of `query`: it also searches every alias listed on their bible page, so references are never under-counted.

query.description: Text or regex to search for (omit when using entity).

entity.description: A character/place name — expands to its bible-page aliases automatically.

regex.description: Treat query as a regular expression (default false).

contextLines.description: Context lines around each match, max 5 (default 1).

tools.name: where_appears
tools.description: Instant answer to 'which scenes is this character/place in?' from the always-fresh entity index: every prose unit the entity (or any of its bible-page aliases) appears in, with mention counts, in narrative order of weight. Cheaper and more complete than searching — use it to orient before drafting or editing anything that involves a known character or place. For line-level matches use search_manuscript instead.

entity.description: The character or place name (any alias from its bible page works).

tools.name: read_project_file
tools.description: Read text from a project-scoped file or line range. Use this to inspect existing content before proposing edits.

fname.description: Project-relative path or absolute path within the active WordBird project.

tools.name: propose_project_file_edit
tools.description: Propose a project-scoped file replacement or line-range edit. This tool must not write directly; it returns an edit proposal for renderer/user review.

fname.description: Project-relative path or absolute path within the active WordBird project.

newdata.description: Replacement content for the whole file or selected range.

start.description: Optional inclusive 1-based start line for range replacement.

end.description: Optional inclusive 1-based end line for range replacement.

reason.description: Optional human-readable explanation for the proposed edit.

tools.name: propose_text_edit
tools.description: THE tool for surgical changes to existing prose: quote the text to replace EXACTLY as it appears in the file (oldText) and provide the replacement (newText) — no line numbers, no whole-file rewrites. oldText must match exactly once: include 2-3 surrounding lines to make it unique, or pass occurrence (1-based). Returns a normal reviewable edit proposal. Use propose_project_file_edit only for full-file rewrites.

oldText.description: The exact existing text to replace — copied verbatim from the file, whitespace and punctuation included.

newText.description: The replacement text (may be empty to delete the span).

reason.description: One line shown to the writer in the review card.

occurrence.description: When oldText appears more than once: which match to edit (1-based).

tools.name: propose_new_unit
tools.description: Add a new part, chapter, or scene to the binder. PUT THE PROSE IN `content` — that is what reaches the writer as a reviewable diff. Without `content` this creates an EMPTY structural shell only (outline work); the synopsis is metadata, never the prose.

parentId.description: Parent unit id (omit for top level).

index.description: Insert position among siblings (appends when omitted).

synopsis.description: One-paragraph synopsis stored as binder metadata.

content.description: The full prose of the new unit — REQUIRED whenever the writer asked for written text. Omitting it saves NO prose (empty shell only). Goes through user review.

tools.name: restructure_unit
tools.description: Move a scene/chapter/part to a new parent and/or position in the binder. Order in the binder is the reading order of the novel.

newParentId.description: Destination parent id (omit for top level).

tools.name: update_unit_meta
tools.description: Update a unit's binder metadata: title, status (idea/draft/revised/final), POV character, location, synopsis, or when (the in-story moment, e.g. 'Day 3' or '1889-06-12', used by the timeline). Does not touch prose. Also sets thread (subplot lane), label (binder keyword), and notes (document notes).

thread.description: Narrative thread/subplot lane this unit belongs to (e.g. "Main", "Heist", "Romance B-plot") — drives the Timeline lanes.

label.description: Writer-defined label/keyword for filtering in the binder (e.g. "act1", "revise").

notes.description: Private writer notes attached to this unit (not prose; visible in the Outline view).

tools.name: read_bible
tools.description: Without a path: list every story-bible page (characters, places, threads, research) with its first line. With a path: read that page in full. ALWAYS consult the bible before writing or editing prose so you stay consistent with established canon.

path.description: Bible-relative file to read in full, e.g. bible/characters/elara.md.

tools.name: propose_bible_update
tools.description: Propose creating or rewriting a story-bible page (must live under bible/). Use this to record new canon facts, character sheets, places, plot threads, or cited research notes. Goes through user review.

path.description: Target page under bible/, e.g. bible/characters/elara.md.

newContent.description: Full new content of the page.

reason.description: Why this canon change/addition is needed.

tools.name: read_summary
tools.description: Read the maintained synopsis for a unit (by id) or the whole book (omit unitId). Prefer summaries over reading full prose when you only need orientation.

unitId.description: Unit id; omit for the book-level summary.

tools.name: update_summary
tools.description: Write the maintained synopsis for a unit (by id) or the whole book (omit unitId). Keep summaries current after prose changes: scene summaries 3-6 sentences, chapter/book summaries proportionally longer.

unitId.description: Unit id; omit for the book-level summary.

tools.name: log_continuity_issue
tools.description: Record a contradiction, timeline problem, dangling setup, or open question you discovered, so the writer can review it later. Include the affected files.

description.description: What conflicts with what, with quotes/locations.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List every file in the project (or a subdirectory) with sizes — notes, research, imports, anything not in the binder. Use this to discover material before reading it.

dir.description: Project-relative directory to list (omit for the whole project).

tools.name: record_fact
tools.description: Record one durable canon fact in the typed story ledger as a subject–relation–object triple (e.g. subject "Zara Voss", relation "eye color", object "grey"). Use during drafting aftercare for facts future scenes must not contradict: physical traits, relationships, dates, injuries, deaths, secrets and who knows them, object locations. Duplicates are ignored. Keep each fact atomic — one triple per call.

subject.description: Who/what the fact is about (character, place, object).

relation.description: The property or relationship (e.g. "eye color", "sister of", "died in").

sourceUnitId.description: Unit id where this fact is established (evidence trail).

tools.name: record_decision
tools.description: Record a SETTLED creative choice with its reason in bible/decisions.md (writer-editable). Use when the writer makes a definitive call ('the sister stays dead', 'never explain the magic on-page') — recorded decisions are never relitigated.

reason.description: Why the writer chose this (optional but valuable).

tools.name: list_decisions
tools.description: List the settled creative decisions (bible/decisions.md). Check BEFORE proposing new directions — never propose against a recorded decision unless the writer re-opens it.

tools.name: project_health
tools.description: Deterministic project-sync report: scenes missing synopsis/status/POV/when/thread (what the corkboard/outline/timeline render), stale summaries, recurring names with no bible page, binder-vs-disk drift, empty-final units, open plan items. Run it FIRST in any coherence/steward pass; fix findings, do not just report them.

tools.name: list_facts
tools.description: Query the typed story-fact ledger. Pass `about` to filter by any word in the subject, relation, or object (e.g. about="Zara" returns every recorded fact touching Zara). Auditors: check new prose against these before approving continuity; drafters: check before asserting canon details.

about.description: Filter facts whose subject/relation/object contains this text (omit for all).

tools.name: lint_prose
tools.description: Deterministic prose checks over one scene or file — the fiction equivalent of running the linter after an edit: doubled words, close repetitions, filler words (very/just/suddenly…), POV filter phrases (she felt/he saw), -ly adverb density, sentence-length stats and monotony, passive-voice share, punctuation hygiene, and any banned terms from bible/style.md. Run it on prose you just drafted or are about to polish; findings are objective SIGNALS to weigh, not laws. Pass exactly one of unitId or fname.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: List the writer's skills (skills/*.md technique files): name, description, file. The brief carries this catalog too; load a body with use_skill when a task matches.

tools.name: use_skill
tools.description: Load a skill's full instructions by name (or filename). Use BEFORE writing when the task matches the skill's description — the writer authored it because they want it followed.

name.description: Skill name from the catalog (or its filename).

tools.name: list_continuity_issues
tools.description: Read all OPEN continuity issues (contradictions, timeline problems, dangling setups) with their ids and affected files. Check this before auditing so you don't re-report known problems.

tools.name: resolve_continuity_issue
tools.description: Mark a continuity issue resolved AFTER verifying the conflict no longer exists in the prose (quote the fixed passage in your resolution note). Never resolve an issue you haven't verified.

resolution.description: How it was verified fixed, with evidence.

tools.name: propose_new_file
tools.description: Propose a brand-new markdown/text file anywhere in the project (notes, research docs, outlines, todo lists). For scenes/chapters use propose_new_unit; for bible pages use propose_bible_update. Goes through user review like every write.

path.description: Project-relative path ending in .md/.txt, e.g. notes/research-questions.md.

content.description: Full content of the new file.

reason.description: Why this file is being created.

tools.name: create_folder
tools.description: Create a folder inside the project (e.g. notes/act-two-research). Files can also create their parent folders implicitly via propose_new_file.

tools.name: move_file
tools.description: Move or rename a file inside the project. A project snapshot is taken first, and if the file backs a binder scene/chapter the manifest is updated automatically so the binder stays intact.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.description: Delete a NON-manuscript file (old notes, dead drafts) after a protective snapshot. Files that back binder units are refused — use delete_unit for those so the manifest stays consistent.

reason.description: Why this file is being removed.

tools.name: delete_unit
tools.description: Remove a unit from the binder (and its files, by default). A project snapshot is taken automatically first so the writer can rewind. Use only when the writer asked for a cut or a restructure requires it.

deleteFiles.description: Also delete the backing files (default true).

reason.description: Why this unit is being removed.

tools.name: wiki_search
tools.description: Search Wikipedia for articles (any language edition). More reliable than general web search for history, geography, science, and biography. Follow up with wiki_read.

lang.description: Wikipedia language code, e.g. en, de, ja (default en).

tools.name: wiki_read
tools.description: Read a Wikipedia article as plain text by its exact title (from wiki_search). Report findings with the returned URL as the citation; the supervisor decides what becomes canon.

refresh.description: Bypass the 7-day content cache and fetch live (only when freshness matters).

tools.name: dictionary_lookup
tools.description: Look up an English word: definitions by part of speech, synonyms, and antonyms. Use when polishing word choice or checking that a word means what the prose needs it to mean.

tools.name: save_research
tools.description: Save durable research findings to bible/research/ so this topic is never re-researched. Cite source URLs. The note is visible to the writer and announced to every future turn under RESEARCH ON FILE.

title.description: Topic title — becomes the note filename.

content.description: The findings, in markdown — conclusions first, then supporting detail.

sources.description: Source URLs the findings came from.

tools.name: save_plan
tools.description: Create a LIVE plan file in plans/ early in a planning conversation. The writer can open and edit it alongside the chat. Keep it current with update_plan as ideas evolve; when it's settled, present it with propose_plan. One plan per task — check list_plans before creating.

title.description: Short plan name, e.g. 'Draft the Amityville short story'.

plan.description: The plan so far, in markdown — numbered steps.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.description: Rewrite an existing plan file as the conversation refines it. The writer may have edited the file themselves — read it first (read_project_file) and fold their changes in rather than clobbering them.

planId.description: Plan path from save_plan/list_plans, e.g. plans/amityville-short-story.md.

title.description: New title (keeps the old one when omitted).

tools.name: list_plans
tools.description: List existing plan files with titles and last-updated times. Use this to decide whether to continue an existing plan (update_plan) or start a fresh one for a new task (save_plan).

tools.name: propose_plan
tools.description: Present a settled plan to the writer as an approval card (reads the CURRENT file, so their manual edits are included). Approving switches them to an execution mode and you'll be asked to carry it out. Call this when planning is done — then stop and wait.

tools.name: start_revision
tools.description: Begin a book-wide revision (removing a character, changing a timeline, renaming across the manuscript). The directive must capture the writer's answers from your interview: what changes, every alias to hunt, who inherits plot functions, delete-vs-rewrite policy, tone constraints. Snapshots the project automatically.

tools.name: get_revision
tools.description: Read a revision's directive, impact map, and progress. EVERY agent working on a revision must call this first so its edits follow the writer's directive.

tools.name: update_impact_map
tools.description: File per-unit findings into a revision's impact map. Classify every affected unit: remove (unit should be cut) | rewrite (substantial changes) | mention-only (trivial reference) | plot-dependency (other storylines depend on this — needs the writer's decision). Include quoted evidence.

evidence.description: Quoted proof this unit is affected.

plan.description: One sentence: what happens to this unit.

tools.name: mark_revision_unit
tools.description: Record progress on one impact-map unit after proposing its edits (done), deciding it needs nothing (skipped), or reopening it (pending). This is how a revision larger than one sitting stays resumable.

tools.name: complete_revision
tools.description: Close a revision after a verification sweep confirms the directive is fully applied (e.g. zero surviving references via search_manuscript entity=…). Refuses while units are still pending unless abandoned=true.

report.description: Verification findings and anything left for the writer.

tools.name: snapshot_project
tools.description: Save a named checkpoint of the entire project (prose + bible) before risky or sweeping work, so the writer can rewind if needed.

message.description: What this snapshot captures, e.g. 'Before renaming Elara'.

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: The project's snapshot history (mini-git): every manual save, every agent batch, every rewind — id, message, timestamp, and whether it was automatic. This is how you see WHEN things changed and find the version to inspect with read_snapshot_file / diff_snapshot_file.

tools.name: read_snapshot_file
tools.displayName: Read a file at a snapshot
tools.description: Read one file exactly as it was at a given snapshot. THE way to recover lost or overwritten prose: read the old version, then propose it back with a normal edit proposal (review-gated) — no project-wide rewind needed.

tools.name: diff_snapshot_file
tools.displayName: Diff a file against a snapshot
tools.description: Unified diff between a file's version at a snapshot and the current working copy — see exactly what changed (writer edits, agent edits, or a rewind) without reading both versions whole.

tools.name: preview_snapshot
tools.description: See a snapshot WITHOUT restoring anything: a project-wide comparison against the current files — which files a restore would revert to older versions, which files written since would be deleted, and which deleted files would come back. ALWAYS run this and report the consequences to the writer before proposing restore_snapshot; it is also the fast answer to "what does that old snapshot look like overall?".

tools.name: restore_snapshot
tools.description: Rewind the ENTIRE project to a snapshot. The writer must approve (every mode), and a safety snapshot of the current state is taken first so the rewind itself is undoable. For a single file, use read_snapshot_file + an edit proposal instead.

snapshotId.description: Snapshot id from list_snapshots to rewind to.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the internet for research (history, geography, science, names, culture). Returns titles, URLs, and snippets. Follow up with web_fetch to read a promising result. Report findings with source URLs; the supervisor decides what becomes canon (bible/research/).

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a public web page and return its readable text (truncated to ~20k characters). Only http(s) URLs; private/local hosts are blocked. Only URLs from the writer or from search results this session can be fetched — never guess a URL, search for it.

refresh.description: Bypass the 7-day content cache and fetch live (only when freshness matters).

tools.name: set_writing_method
tools.description: Record how the writer likes to work, after THEY tell you. planningStyle: outline-first (plotter), discovery (pantser, never push outlines), hybrid. structureTemplate seeds a beat sheet at bible/structure.md (three-act, save-the-cat, heros-journey, seven-point, romancing-the-beat, or freeform for none). Metadata only — changeable any time; the writer's words always win over the recorded method.

structureTemplate.description: Story structure framework; seeds bible/structure.md unless freeform.

tools.name: ask_writer
tools.description: Ask the writer ONE question with selectable options — renders as a card with buttons plus a free-form field. Use whenever the choices are enumerable (genre, tone, POV, picking between premises, yes/no forks) instead of writing a wall of questions. Put your recommended option FIRST and mark it. After calling this, END your turn and wait for the answer.

label.description: Short answer text (becomes the writer's reply).
